questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to write the scientific name of the mango?
questions.explain: Capital genus, lower-case species, in italics.

questions.prompt: In which kingdom are bacteria placed?
Put the ranks in order from the biggest group to the smallest.
questions.explain: Each rank contains the ones below it.

questions.prompt: Which kingdom has organisms with cell walls made of chitin that absorb their food?
questions.explain: Fungi are saprophytes with chitin walls.

options: A group of similar organisms that can breed together to produce fertile offspring
All the animals in a habitat
questions.explain: The ability to produce fertile offspring defines a species.

questions.prompt: Amoeba is single-celled and has a nucleus. Which kingdom is it in?
Two animals are in the same family but different genera. Two others are in the same order but different families. Which pair is more closely related?
options: The pair in the same family
The pair in the same order
questions.explain: Family is a lower (smaller) rank than order.

questions.prompt: Explain two advantages of giving every species a scientific name.
questions.modelAnswer: A scientific name is the same everywhere in the world, so scientists speaking different languages know exactly which species is meant; local common names vary and can refer to several species. The name also shows relationships: the genus name groups closely related species together (e.g. Panthera tigris and Panthera leo).
rubric: Universal: avoids confusion between languages or local names
